questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Define a Roll-Up Summary Field

questions.question: What is the maximum number of roll-up summary fields allowed per object?

options.text: Unlimited

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Salesforce limits each object to 25 roll-up summary fields. Custom app packaging can increase this only in rare cases. A, C, and D are incorrect.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Roll-Up Summary Field Limits

questions.scenario: A developer notes that a roll-up summary field is not updating in real time when the child records are edited via Data Loader.
questions.question: What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Roll-up summary fields do not fire when records are updated via API without workflow triggers
Roll-up summary fields are recalculated on save, but very large operations may require a manual force recalculation
Data Loader cannot trigger roll-up summary recalculation
Roll-up summary fields only update from the Salesforce UI

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Roll-up summaries normally recalculate automatically on save, but very large or bulk operations may skip real-time recalculation; admins can force recalculation from Setup. A, C, and D are false — roll-ups do fire from API-based inserts/updates like Data Loader.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Recalculate Roll-Up Summary Values

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks has a master-detail relationship from Order to Order Line Item. They want a roll-up summary that averages line item Discount %.
questions.question: How should the App Builder achieve this?

options.text: Create a roll-up summary that averages Discount__c
Create two roll-ups (SUM of Discount, COUNT of Line Items) and use a formula field to divide them
Roll-up summaries do not support decimal fields
Use MIN on the Discount field

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Roll-up summary fields do not support AVG. A common workaround is to roll up SUM and COUNT, then divide with a formula field. A is wrong — AVG is not supported. C is false — decimals are supported. D would return the smallest value, not the average.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Roll-Up Summary Field Types

questions.question: When does a validation rule prevent a record from being saved?

options.text: When the error condition formula evaluates to TRUE
When the error condition formula evaluates to FALSE
When the record fails a lookup filter
When the user lacks Modify All permission

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. A validation rule blocks the save when its error condition formula returns TRUE (i.e., the invalid condition is met). B is the opposite. C and D are unrelated to validation rules.

questions.scenario: Universal Containers wants to prevent users from setting Opportunity Stage to Closed Won unless the Amount is greater than 0.
questions.question: Which validation rule formula is correct?

options.text: AND(ISPICKVAL(StageName,'Closed Won'), OR(ISBLANK(Amount), Amount <= 0))
IF(StageName='Closed Won', Amount > 0, FALSE)
NOT(ISPICKVAL(StageName,'Closed Won')) AND Amount > 0
ISPICKVAL(StageName,'Closed Won') AND Amount > 0

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The rule blocks save when Stage is Closed Won AND Amount is blank or 0 — the invalid combination. B is wrong because IF returning FALSE never blocks the save. C is inverted. D would block valid records (Closed Won with an Amount).

questions.question: Where can a validation rule display its error message?

options.text: Only at the top of the page
Only on a specific field
At the top of the page OR on a specific field
In a modal dialog after Save

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Validation rules can display errors at the top of the page or attached to a specific field. A and B are individually incomplete. D is not an option.

questions.scenario: AW Computing wants system administrators to bypass a validation rule when running data loads while regular users must still be blocked.
questions.question: What is the recommended declarative approach?

options.text: Add $Profile.Name to the formula and exclude 'System Administrator'
Create a custom permission (e.g., Bypass_Validation) and reference $Permission.Bypass_Validation in the formula
Deactivate the validation rule during loads and reactivate it after
Use a validation rule bypass hierarchy setting in Setup

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The best practice is to create a Custom Permission granted via a permission set, then reference $Permission in the validation rule to bypass it. This scales without hard-coded profile names. A is fragile and profile-dependent. C is risky and manual. D is not a real Salesforce feature.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Custom Permissions in Formulas

questions.question: At what point in the order of execution do validation rules run?

options.text: Before-save flows and validation rules run in the same block, before after-save triggers
After after-save triggers
Only after all workflow field updates complete
Only after commit to the database

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Validation rules run after before-save triggers/flows and before after-save triggers. They execute after system validation and before commit. B, C, and D misplace them in the order of execution.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Triggers and Order of Execution

questions.scenario: DreamHouse Realty needs a validation rule that prevents a Contact from being saved if the Email field is not in a valid email format.
questions.question: Which function should be used?

options.text: The standard Email field type already validates format — no rule needed
ISNULL(Email)

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Email fields in Salesforce inherently validate format at save time; adding a regex validation rule is redundant. B could work for a Text field but is unnecessary here. A is incomplete. D only checks blankness.

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks wants to automatically update the Description field on a Case whenever the record is created, using values from other fields on the same record. Performance is important.
questions.question: Which type of flow should the App Builder use?

options.text: Record-Triggered Flow, After-Save
Record-Triggered Flow, Before-Save
Screen Flow
Scheduled Flow

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Before-save record-triggered flows update fields on the triggering record without an additional DML operation — the fastest and cheapest option. A works but is slower because it requires an extra DML. C requires user interaction. D runs on a schedule, not on record create.

questions.scenario: Universal Containers wants a flow that fires when an Account is updated, and creates a Task on a related Contact.
questions.question: Which flow configuration should be used?

options.text: Record-Triggered Flow, Before-Save on Account
Record-Triggered Flow, After-Save on Account
Schedule-Triggered Flow, daily
Platform Event-Triggered Flow

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Creating related records requires an after-save record-triggered flow. Before-save flows cannot create other records. A is wrong for that reason. C batches once per schedule, not real time. D requires publishing platform events explicitly.

questions.question: Which are best practices for building record-triggered flows? (Choose 2)

options.text: Use Get Records inside a Loop
Use Assignment elements to build collections outside the loop, then a single Update/Create Records after the loop
Use Fault paths on DML elements to handle errors gracefully
Deploy flows as Active in production without testing in a sandbox first
Create one flow per object per trigger — avoid the recommended single-flow pattern

questions.explanation: The correct answers are B and C. Bulkification (moving DML outside loops) and adding Fault paths are core best practices. A causes governor-limit issues. D is dangerous. E contradicts Salesforce's guidance to use one flow per object per trigger context, split logically by criteria.

questions.scenario: An App Builder needs to loop through a collection of Contacts and check whether each one meets a criterion.
questions.question: Which flow element should be used to evaluate the criterion inside the loop?

options.text: Assignment
Decision
Get Records
Subflow

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. A Decision element evaluates conditions and routes flow logic accordingly. A stores values but doesn't branch. C queries data. D calls other flows. Only Decision can branch based on criteria.

questions.question: Which flow resource is used to store a group of records or values of the same data type?

options.text: Variable
Formula
Collection variable
Constant

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Collection variables store multiple values or records of the same type — key to bulkifying flows. A holds a single value. B calculates a value at runtime. D is a read-only fixed value.

questions.scenario: A record-triggered flow updates Opportunity records. Some updates fail due to a validation rule. The App Builder wants to log the failures and continue processing the rest.
questions.question: Which flow capability should be used?

options.text: Add a Fault path to the Update Records element
Use Roll Back Records to revert everything
Deactivate the validation rule during the flow
Wrap the Update in a Try/Catch element

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Fault paths let a flow branch on DML errors so admins can log and continue. B rolls back the whole transaction. C is not possible mid-flow. D — flows don't have Try/Catch elements; Fault paths serve that role.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Fault Connectors and Paths

questions.scenario: Ursa Major Solar has a complex record-triggered flow that must call external APIs and handle results without blocking the user save.
questions.question: Which flow trigger type should be used?

options.text: Before-Save Record-Triggered Flow
After-Save Record-Triggered Flow
Record-Triggered Flow with Asynchronous Path
Screen Flow

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. Asynchronous paths run after the transaction commits and support external callouts, which are not allowed in the synchronous transaction. A cannot make callouts. B cannot make callouts synchronously either. D requires user interaction.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Asynchronous Paths in Record-Triggered Flows

questions.scenario: AW Computing wants to send a welcome email to new Contacts when they are created, using a Salesforce Classic email template.
questions.question: Which flow action should be used?

options.text: Send Email action
Send Email Alert action referencing a defined email alert
HTTP Callout
Post to Chatter

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The Send Email Alert action leverages configured email alerts, including recipient logic and templates. A can send simple emails but doesn't use configured email alerts. C is for API calls. D posts to Chatter feeds, not email.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Email Actions in Flow

questions.question: In Flow Builder, which element allows one flow to invoke another flow?

options.text: Action
Subflow
Recursion
Loop

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Subflow elements invoke autolaunched or screen flows from another flow, supporting reuse. A invokes an Apex/other action. C is not a flow element. D iterates through collections.

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks wants a flow to prompt users for input and update related records based on responses.
questions.question: Which flow type is required?

options.text: Screen Flow
Autolaunched Flow
Record-Triggered Flow
Platform Event-Triggered Flow

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Screen Flows are the only flow type that supports user input via Screen elements. B and C run without user interaction. D reacts to events.

questions.scenario: A record-triggered flow contains a loop with Update Records inside it. Every time bulk updates happen, the flow fails with governor limit errors.
questions.question: What is the recommended remediation?

options.text: Move the Update Records outside the loop and pass in a collection variable
Split the flow into multiple flows
Convert the flow to Apex
Add a Pause element inside the loop

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Bulkification (single DML operating on a collection) is the primary way to avoid governor limits. B may not help. C is unnecessary — Flow can bulkify. D pauses are for waits, not governor limit avoidance and cause other issues.

questions.question: Which flow features can throw custom errors to a user? (Choose 2)

options.text: Custom Error element in a record-triggered flow
Validation rule created inside the flow
A Screen Flow with a validation formula on a Screen input
Assignment element that sets a message variable
Formula field returning an error message

questions.explanation: The correct answers are A and C. The Custom Error element (record-triggered flows) and Screen input validation both display errors to the user. B is a separate feature, not created in a flow. D just stores a value — it does not display an error. E returns text but doesn't block a save.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Custom Error in Flow

questions.scenario: A screen flow needs to display a table of Cases the user can select from and pass the selected ID onward.
questions.question: Which screen component enables this?

options.text: Data Table
Radio Buttons
Rich Text Field
Toggle

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The Data Table screen component in Screen Flow displays record collections with selection support. B lists options but not record rows. C is for static content. D is a boolean toggle.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Data Table Screen Component

questions.scenario: A record-triggered flow must roll back all its changes and display a user-friendly error if a validation condition fails mid-flow.
questions.question: Which flow element should be used?

options.text: Custom Error element
Roll Back Records element followed by Decision
Update Records with fault path
Pause element with error condition

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The Custom Error element throws a user-facing error and rolls back the entire transaction, replacing the older approach of Roll Back Records + manual error handling. B works but Custom Error is the modern, preferred method. C only handles errors, doesn't roll back. D is a wait, not a stop-and-error.

questions.question: Which flow resource type is used to store a value that never changes during flow execution?

options.text: Variable
Constant
Formula
Choice

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Constants are read-only fixed values in a flow. A allows updates. C is calculated at runtime. D provides selectable choices.

questions.question: Salesforce Winter '23 Retired which tools for creating new automations?

options.text: Workflow Rules and Process Builder
Approval Processes and Flow
Apex Triggers and Apex Classes
Validation Rules and Formula Fields

Existing ones can still run, but new automations should be built in Flow. Migrations are supported via the Migrate to Flow tool. B, C, and D are still fully supported.

questions.scenario: Universal Containers has hundreds of legacy Workflow Rules and Process Builder processes and wants to migrate them to Flow.
questions.question: Which Salesforce-provided tool should be used?

Data Import Wizard
Change Set
Setup Audit Trail

questions.question: Which flow element makes an outbound REST callout to an external service without writing code?

options.text: HTTP Callout element (invoked via External Service)
Post to Chatter
Send Custom Notification
Roll Back Records

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The HTTP Callout flow element enables declarative REST API callouts to Named Credentials/External Services. B is for social feeds. C sends in-app notifications. D reverts DML.

questions.scenario: A Screen Flow needs a variable that the user cannot see, but which the flow needs to compute intermediate values.
questions.question: How should the App Builder configure this variable?

options.text: Set the variable's Availability Outside the Flow to Input Only
Uncheck 'Available for input' and 'Available for output'
Set the variable's Data Type to Apex-defined
Assign the variable to a Screen field with visibility hidden

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. If a variable does not need to be passed in from a parent flow or made available externally, unchecking input/output access hides it from the caller. A exposes it as input. C changes datatype, not visibility. D exposes it via UI.

questions.question: Which scenarios should NOT be handled by Flow and should instead use Apex? (Choose 2)

Complex, recursive computations over thousands of records synchronously
Advanced integration logic requiring dynamic parsing of JSON/XML
Sending a Chatter post when a Case is created
Assigning a new Case Owner using simple criteria

questions.scenario: A record-triggered flow needs to route on multiple conditions (New, Escalated, Closed) and take different paths for each.

options.text: Multiple stacked Decision elements
A single Decision element with multiple outcomes
A Loop with nested Decisions
A Subflow for each condition

questions.question: What is a Flow Interview?

A template for building conversational flows
The design-time editor for a flow
A user's answers to Screen inputs

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks needs a flow that runs every night at 2 AM to archive Cases older than one year.

Record-Triggered Flow
Screen Flow
Platform Event-Triggered Flow

questions.scenario: Universal Containers wants a flow that subscribes to a Platform Event named Order_Placed__e and creates a related Order record.

Record-Triggered Flow on Order

questions.scenario: DreamHouse Realty wants a flow that can be launched from Apex code or a REST call, without requiring user input or record trigger.

options.text: Autolaunched Flow (no trigger)
Screen Flow
Record-Triggered Flow
Schedule-Triggered Flow

questions.scenario: AW Computing wants to update fields on the same record just before it is saved. Performance is critical.
questions.question: Which flow type should be used?

options.text: Record-Triggered Flow, Before-Save
Record-Triggered Flow, After-Save
Screen Flow
Autolaunched Flow

questions.scenario: Ursa Major Solar needs a flow that fires when a Data Cloud Data Model Object receives new records that meet certain criteria.
questions.question: Which flow type should be used?

options.text: Data Cloud-Triggered Flow
Journey-Triggered Flow
Record-Triggered Flow
Platform Event-Triggered Flow

questions.question: Which flow trigger type supports scheduling a run at a specific time in the future for a specific record?

options.text: Scheduled Paths in a Record-Triggered Flow
Schedule-Triggered Flow
Platform Event-Triggered Flow
Before-Save Trigger

questions.question: Which flow types are considered autolaunched (no user interaction)? (Choose 2)

Screen Flow
Record-Triggered Flow
Contact Request Flow
Field Service Mobile Flow

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks wants to run heavy business logic when an Opportunity is closed won, but does not need the logic to complete before the user sees the save confirmation.

options.text: Record-Triggered Flow with an Asynchronous Path

questions.scenario: An App Builder is deciding whether to build a scheduled flow or a record-triggered flow to update stale records nightly.

options.text: Schedule-Triggered Flow with a filter for stale records
Record-Triggered Flow on every record update
Screen Flow launched from Lightning App
Manual Data Loader run each night

Sales Cloud
Service Cloud Voice
Data Cloud

questions.question: Universal Containers wants to build a modern approval process using declarative tools. Which is the recommended approach for a new build?

Classic Approval Processes only
Process Builder
Workflow Rules

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Approval Orchestrations in Flow (via Flow Orchestrator) are the modern declarative approach and support multi-stage, multi-user workflows. B still works but is legacy. C and D are retired for new automations.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Flow Orchestrator and Approval Orchestrations

questions.question: In a classic Approval Process, what happens if the final approver approves the record?

options.text: The Final Approval Actions are executed
The record is deleted
The record is submitted again
Nothing happens automatically

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Once the final approver approves, Final Approval Actions defined on the approval process run (e.g., field updates, email alerts). B, C, D are incorrect.

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks needs an approver's designated backup to be able to approve on their behalf when they are on vacation.
questions.question: Which approval feature supports this?

options.text: Delegated Approver setting on User records
Custom Permission on the approval process
Sharing rule for approval history
Field-level security override

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. A Delegated Approver can approve items assigned to another user. B, C, and D do not enable delegated approval.

questions.question: Which of the following is a valid approver type in an Approval Process step?

options.text: Related User (a User lookup field on the record)
Public Group
Role hierarchy above submitter
All of the above

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Approval steps can route to a specific user, related User field, Queue, Public Group, Role, or role hierarchy above the submitter. All listed options are valid.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Approval Process Approver Types

questions.question: Which are TRUE about recalling an approval request? (Choose 2)

options.text: The submitter can recall a pending request if 'Allow Submitters to Recall Approval Requests' is enabled
Recall Actions defined on the approval process execute automatically upon recall
Once approved, the record can still be recalled
Recall bypasses all validation rules
Only the current approver can recall the request

questions.explanation: The correct answers are A and B. Submitters can recall pending approvals if the option is enabled, and Recall Actions execute automatically. C is false — recall applies to pending requests. D is false. E is false — submitters (and admins) can recall.

questions.scenario: AW Computing wants approvers to have a specified time window (e.g., 3 business days) to approve. If not approved by then, the request should escalate.
questions.question: Which approval process feature enables this?

options.text: Approval Automated Approver Response Rules
Response Timeout and Escalation Steps
Delegated Approver time settings
Time-based Workflow Rules on the approval history

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Approval processes support response timeouts and can automatically send the request to a higher-level approver if not acted upon in time. A is not a real feature. C is unrelated. D is retired for new automations.

questions.question: Where can an administrator monitor paused and failed flow interviews?

options.text: Setup → Paused and Waiting Interviews and the Flow Interviews list
Only via Debug Logs
In a custom report on Flow Interview object
In the Flow Builder canvas

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Setup includes Paused and Waiting Interviews plus the standard Flow Interviews list for monitoring in-progress interviews. B provides logs but not the monitoring view. C is possible but not the standard admin path. D shows design, not runtime.

questions.question: By default, who receives flow error emails when an unhandled error occurs?

options.text: The user who launched the flow
The flow owner (Apex Exception Email or Flow error setting recipient)
The System Administrator profile users
Salesforce Support

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Flow errors default to the running user or the addresses configured via Process Automation Settings / Apex Exception Email. A is only partially correct depending on org settings. C and D are not defaults.

questions.scenario: An App Builder wants to test a flow's logic against a real record to see step-by-step execution before deploying.
questions.question: Which Flow Builder feature should be used?

options.text: Debug
Deploy
Activate
Run

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. The Debug feature in Flow Builder allows the App Builder to run a flow with specific inputs and see element-by-element execution. B pushes changes elsewhere. C makes the version live. D just runs it without inspection.

questions.question: How does flow versioning work?

options.text: Each save creates a new draft; only one version can be Active at a time
Every change immediately overwrites the previous version
All versions are Active simultaneously
Version numbers must be manually assigned

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Each save creates a new version (or updates a draft), but only one version can be Active per flow. B, C, and D describe non-existent behavior.

questions.question: Which Salesforce feature allows an admin to write reusable automated tests for a Screen Flow?

options.text: Flow Tests
Apex Tests
Debug Log
Flow Interviews

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Flow Tests let admins define test scenarios with inputs and expected outputs for screen and record-triggered flows. B is code-based. C is a diagnostic log, not test framework. D is runtime instance monitoring.

questions.question: When deploying flows between orgs, which are TRUE? (Choose 2)

options.text: Flow versions can be deployed as either Active or Draft (with deployment settings)
Deploying a new Active version deactivates the previous Active version automatically
Flow test coverage requirements apply to production deployments similar to Apex
Deployed flows always require re-authoring in the target org
Change Sets do not support Flow deployment

questions.explanation: The correct answers are A and B. Deployment settings allow deploying active flows, and activating a new version deactivates the old one automatically. C is false — Flow Tests are recommended but not required by the platform for production deployment. D is false. E is false — Change Sets support flow deployment.

questions.scenario: An App Builder wants to review debug logs generated by an autolaunched flow's runtime.
questions.question: How can the App Builder capture these logs?

options.text: Set a debug trace flag for the running user and open the debug log
Enable audit trail
Read Flow Interviews list from Setup only
Trigger a Chatter post from the flow

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Debug logs, triggered via trace flags for the running user, capture flow execution details. B tracks setup changes, not flow runtime. C is a monitoring view. D is unrelated.

questions.question: What is Agentforce?

options.text: Salesforce's AI agent platform, built on Einstein 1, that automates business tasks through actions and topics
A replacement for Salesforce Flows
The successor to Process Builder for record-triggered automation
A tool for creating custom Lightning components

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Agentforce is Salesforce's platform for autonomous and assistive AI agents built on the Einstein 1 platform (formerly branded as Einstein Copilot). It leverages topics and actions to complete tasks. B, C, and D are incorrect — Agentforce augments, does not replace, flow-based automation and is not for LWC.

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks wants Agentforce to be able to create a Case for a customer via natural language chat.
questions.question: Which Agentforce component defines how Agentforce performs this task?

options.text: Agent Action (Standard or Custom)
Screen Flow only
Static Resource
Sharing Rule

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Agent Actions define discrete tasks that an agent can perform. A custom action can invoke a Flow, Apex, or Prompt Template. B could be the implementation but the concept exposed to the agent is an Action. C is a static file store. D is record sharing.

questions.question: Which of the following can be invoked as an Agentforce Action?

options.text: Autolaunched Flow
Apex Method
Prompt Template
All of the above

questions.explanation: The correct answer is D. Agentforce actions can invoke Autolaunched Flows, Apex methods, and Prompt Templates. All of these are supported implementations behind an agent action.

questions.scenario: Ursa Major Solar wants a service agent to deflect common questions using generative AI and Salesforce Knowledge articles.
questions.question: Which Agentforce feature and configuration is best?

options.text: A Service Agent grounded on Knowledge with an Answer Questions action
A Screen Flow with a Rich Text field
A record-triggered flow on Case
A validation rule on Contact

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Agentforce Service Agents can be grounded on Knowledge articles and use generative actions to answer customer questions, deflecting cases. B, C, and D do not use generative AI for deflection.

questions.question: What is a 'Topic' in Agentforce?

options.text: A grouping of related actions and instructions that helps an agent understand when to invoke them
A Chatter feed category
A subject line for email alerts
A prompt template variable

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Topics organize actions and instructions in Agentforce, giving the agent context on when to use particular capabilities. B, C, and D are unrelated concepts.

questions.scenario: AW Computing wants Agentforce to draft personalized outreach emails using data from Contact and Account records.
questions.question: Which Salesforce feature enables generative content grounded in CRM data for an Agentforce action?

options.text: Prompt Builder Prompt Template referenced by an Agentforce action
Email Template with merge fields only
Formula field with TEXT() concatenation
Apex trigger

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Prompt Builder templates ground LLM prompts with Salesforce data via merge fields and can be invoked by Agentforce actions to generate personalized content. B is static merge only. C is limited. D doesn't use generative AI.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common use case where Agentforce complements traditional Flow automation?

options.text: Interpreting free-form user requests and calling the right underlying flow
Enforcing field-level security
Storing static reference data
Replacing sharing rules

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Agentforce agents translate natural-language user intent into structured actions that call flows, Apex, or prompt templates. B is a security feature. C is data storage. D is record access.

questions.scenario: An App Builder wants a flow to pause for 24 hours before continuing execution on a specific record.
questions.question: Which flow feature should be used?

options.text: Scheduled Path in a Record-Triggered Flow
Loop with counter
Subflow
Assignment element

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Scheduled Paths let a record-triggered flow pause and resume at a specified offset (e.g., 24 hours). B, C, and D cannot wait for elapsed time.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Scheduled Paths in Flow

questions.scenario: DreamHouse Realty wants a formula that returns different text values based on Region: 'North' → 'N', 'South' → 'S', 'East' → 'E', 'West' → 'W', default 'Other'.
questions.question: Which function is most efficient?

options.text: CASE(Region__c, 'North', 'N', 'South', 'S', 'East', 'E', 'West', 'W', 'Other')
Nested IF statements four levels deep
Concatenated TEXT() functions
VLOOKUP formula

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. CASE evaluates one expression against multiple possible values with a default — cleaner and more efficient than nested IFs. B works but is harder to maintain. C doesn't map values. D is not standard in Salesforce (VLOOKUP exists only for validation rule cross-object lookups).

questions.question: Which are limits or considerations for record-triggered flows? (Choose 2)

options.text: They are subject to per-transaction governor limits like SOQL and DML
Before-save flows can call Apex actions and external callouts
Async paths can perform external HTTP callouts
Record-triggered flows can bypass validation rules automatically
Record-triggered flows only run in Sandbox orgs

questions.explanation: The correct answers are A and C. All flows are subject to per-transaction governor limits. Only async paths (not sync before/after-save) can perform HTTP callouts. B is false — before-save can't call Apex actions or external services. D is false — flows honor validation rules. E is false.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Flow Limits and Considerations

questions.scenario: Universal Containers wants to detect changes to an Opportunity Amount field and enforce a business rule based on the previous value.
questions.question: Which formula function references the prior value of a field?

options.text: PRIORVALUE(Amount)
OLDVALUE(Amount)
PREVIOUS(Amount)
ISCHANGED(Amount)

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. PRIORVALUE() returns the previous value of a field in a validation rule or workflow. B, C are not valid Salesforce functions. D detects whether a value changed but doesn't return the prior value.

questions.question: Which are TRUE about invoking automation from an Agentforce agent? (Choose 2)

options.text: A custom Agent Action can wrap an Autolaunched Flow and call it with input parameters
Only Apex classes can serve as custom Agent Actions
Prompt Templates can be surfaced as generative Agent Actions
Agentforce cannot call server-side Salesforce automation
All Agent Actions require an active Marketing Cloud connection

questions.explanation: The correct answers are A and C. Agentforce custom actions can wrap Autolaunched Flows and Prompt Templates (in addition to Apex). B is false — Flows and Prompts are also supported. D is false — Agentforce is built to invoke Salesforce automation. E is false — Marketing Cloud is not required.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Building Custom Agent Actions

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks wants sales reps to see key Opportunity fields displayed in the highlights panel at the top of the record page and in the hover card when they mouse over an opportunity link.
questions.question: Which layout should the App Builder configure to control the fields displayed in these locations?

options.text: Page Layout
Compact Layout
Search Layout
Mini Page Layout

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Compact layouts control the key fields shown in the highlights panel, hover cards, and mobile record cards. A (Page Layout) controls the full detail area of a record but not the highlights panel. C (Search Layout) controls list view columns and search result columns, not highlights. D (Mini Page Layout) was a Classic construct used in hover details and is not the mechanism in Lightning Experience.

questions.scenario: Ursa Major Solar's admin wants field-level visibility on the Account record page to change based on the value of the Account Type field, without cloning multiple page layouts.
questions.question: Which feature should the admin use?

options.text: Record Types with different page layouts
Dynamic Forms with field-level visibility rules
A Visualforce page with rendered conditions
Validation Rules on the Account object

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Dynamic Forms let you place individual fields onto a Lightning record page and apply visibility rules based on field values, user attributes, or device — eliminating the need for multiple page layouts. A works but is heavy-handed and requires cloning layouts. C is a programmatic solution and unnecessary. D governs data validation, not field visibility.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Break Up Your Record Details with Dynamic Forms

questions.scenario: AW Computing wants to launch a new Lightning App for its Service team that includes a persistent tray at the bottom of the screen with quick access to Notes, History, and Omni-Channel.
questions.question: Which Lightning App feature provides this persistent tray?

options.text: App Manager
Utility Bar
Navigation Bar
Chatter Publisher

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The Utility Bar is a horizontal footer available on Lightning apps (both standard and console navigation) that provides quick, persistent access to utilities like Notes, History, and Omni-Channel. A (App Manager) is the Setup tool where you create/edit Lightning Apps, not the tray itself. C (Navigation Bar) is the top bar of tabs. D (Chatter Publisher) is a component for posting to Chatter feeds.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Utility Bar for Lightning Apps

questions.scenario: NTO's administrator is configuring a new Lightning App for the customer support team. Agents need to work on multiple Cases at once, keeping each Case open in a separate workspace tab.
questions.question: Which two configurations should the admin choose for this app? (Choose 2)

options.text: Set the Navigation Style to 'Console'
Set the Navigation Style to 'Standard'
Add a Utility Bar with Omni-Channel and Notes
Enable Person Accounts

questions.explanation: The correct answers are A and C. Console navigation opens each record in a workspace tab with subtabs — ideal for support agents multi-tasking on Cases. A Utility Bar (available on both Standard and Console apps but especially useful in Console) gives persistent access to Omni-Channel and Notes. B (Standard navigation) opens records one at a time. D (Person Accounts) is unrelated to app navigation.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Console Navigation for Lightning Apps

questions.scenario: DreamHouse Realty wants the Property record page to show a Google Map component only when the Property Status field equals 'Active Listing'.
questions.question: How should the App Builder configure this?

options.text: Create a formula field that hides the map when the status is not Active Listing
Add a Component Visibility filter on the map component in Lightning App Builder
Write an Apex controller to conditionally render the map
Create two separate page layouts assigned by record type

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Every component on a Lightning record page supports Component Visibility filters based on record field values, user attributes, form factor, or permission — no code required. A doesn't control component visibility. C is programmatic and unnecessary. D would work but is heavier and doesn't leverage Lightning App Builder's built-in feature.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Dynamic Lightning Pages with Component Visibility

questions.question: Which tool in Setup lets an admin create, clone, and manage Lightning Apps for standard and console navigation?

options.text: Lightning App Builder
App Manager
Object Manager
Setup Home

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. App Manager in Setup is where admins create, edit, and clone Lightning Apps, including navigation style, utility bar items, and user profiles. A (Lightning App Builder) is used to build Lightning Pages (record, home, app pages), not the Apps themselves. C manages objects and their fields. D is the general Setup landing page.

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks wants to guide new sales reps through the sales process by showing them the current opportunity stage, key fields to complete, and coaching tips at each step, directly on the Opportunity record page.
questions.question: Which standard Lightning component should the App Builder add to the Opportunity record page?

options.text: Related List — Single
Rich Text
Path
Recommendations

questions.explanation: The correct answer is C. The Path component visually displays the stages of the sales process and lets admins configure Key Fields and Guidance for Success at each stage. A displays a single related list. B is for static rich text content. D (Recommendations) surfaces Einstein-based next-best actions or admin-defined recommendations, but does not show stage progress.

questions.scenario: Universal Containers is migrating a standard object's record page from classic page layouts to Dynamic Forms.
questions.question: Which two statements about Dynamic Forms are TRUE in Summer '26? (Choose 2)

options.text: Dynamic Forms replace the Record Detail component with Field Section components you can place anywhere on the page
Dynamic Forms remove the need for page layouts entirely across the org, including for lead conversion mapping and search layouts
Dynamic Forms support visibility rules on individual fields and field sections
Dynamic Forms are only supported on custom objects

questions.explanation: The correct answers are A and C. Dynamic Forms let you swap the monolithic Record Detail for individual Field Sections and fields on the Lightning record page, and you can apply visibility rules on each. B is false — page layouts are still used for other purposes (compact/related-list influence, lead conversion mapping, mobile card layout, etc.). D is false — Dynamic Forms is GA for standard objects (rolled out over multiple releases) and is now recommended across the platform.

questions.scenario: Ursa Major Solar wants to display a Salesforce report chart directly on the Account record page so reps can see year-to-date revenue for that account.
questions.question: Which standard component should the admin drag onto the record page?

options.text: Rich Text
Report Chart
Related Record
Dashboard

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. The Report Chart component embeds a chart from a Salesforce report on a Lightning page, with filters that can respect the current record's ID. A displays formatted text. C displays fields from a related record inline. D is not a standard component available in Lightning App Builder for a record page in this way — dashboards live on their own pages.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Standard Lightning Page Components

questions.scenario: AW Computing wants an in-app walkthrough that guides new users through creating their first Opportunity, without writing any code.
questions.question: Which feature should the admin use?

options.text: In-App Guidance
myTrailhead
Path with Guidance for Success
A custom Lightning component

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. In-App Guidance lets admins create prompts and walkthroughs that appear at specific places in Lightning Experience, targeting user profiles and permissions — all declarative. B is a learning content platform (deprecated for new customers). C helps users progress through a record's stages but doesn't provide multi-step walkthroughs across the app. D would work but is programmatic and unnecessary.

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks wants the login page and internal Lightning Experience navigation bar to reflect its brand colors and logo.
questions.question: Which Setup area should the admin use for the internal Lightning Experience branding?

options.text: Themes and Branding
Experience Builder
Static Resources
Custom Metadata Types

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Themes and Branding (in Setup) lets admins customize the Lightning Experience look — brand image, colors for the navigation bar, links, and background — and activate a theme. B is used for external Experience Cloud sites. C stores files but doesn't apply theme colors. D is a metadata configuration tool unrelated to visual theming.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Themes and Branding in Lightning Experience

questions.scenario: DreamHouse Realty added Dynamic Forms to the Property record page but is now getting reports that some fields don't show up on the Salesforce mobile app.
questions.question: What is the most likely cause?

options.text: Dynamic Forms require a permission set for mobile users
The mobile record page uses a separate Lightning page assignment and must be updated to use Dynamic Forms
Dynamic Forms are not supported on the Salesforce mobile app for standard objects
The compact layout has not been updated

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Lightning record pages have separate assignments for Desktop and Phone. If the mobile Lightning page assignment still points to a page that uses the classic Record Detail component (not Dynamic Forms), users will see the legacy layout. A is incorrect — no such permission set. C is false — Dynamic Forms is supported on mobile. D affects highlights/hover cards, not the record page body.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Dynamic Forms on Mobile

questions.scenario: NTO wants a button on the Account record page that creates a related Case with the Account already populated.
questions.question: Which is the recommended declarative approach?

options.text: Custom URL button with a URL hack
Object-specific Quick Action of type 'Create a Record'
Global Action of type 'Create a Record'
Custom Visualforce button

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. An object-specific 'Create a Record' Quick Action on Account can create a related Case and automatically populate the AccountId. A (URL hacks) are unsupported in Lightning Experience. C would create a standalone Case without linking to the current Account context. D is programmatic and unnecessary.

questions.question: Which statement about Global Actions is TRUE?

options.text: Global Actions can only create records for the current object context
Global Actions are available from the Global Publisher Layout, including the Chatter publisher and the navigation bar Actions menu
Global Actions cannot log a call or send email
Global Actions can only be created by developers

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Global Actions can be launched from anywhere in the app — the Chatter publisher, the '+' menu in the navigation bar, and mobile — because they aren't tied to a specific record's context. A describes object-specific actions. C is false — Log a Call and Send Email are supported Global Action types. D is false — admins configure them declaratively.

questions.scenario: Universal Containers has a legacy custom button on the Case object built with a JavaScript URL hack that populates fields on the new record page. Users report the button no longer works in Lightning Experience.
questions.question: What should the App Builder do?

options.text: Rewrite the JavaScript to be Lightning-compatible
Replace it with a Quick Action of type 'Create a Record' with predefined field values
Add the JavaScript button to a Visualforce page and embed it
Enable JavaScript buttons in Session Settings

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. JavaScript buttons and URL hacks are not supported in Lightning Experience. The declarative replacement is a Quick Action (typically 'Create a Record') with predefined field values on the action layout — no code required. A, C, and D are not viable — Lightning doesn't run legacy JavaScript buttons regardless of workaround.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Convert JavaScript Buttons to Lightning Alternatives

questions.question: Where do admins define which fields appear on a Quick Action's create/update form?

options.text: The Page Layout of the parent object
The Action Layout of the Quick Action
The Compact Layout of the target object
The Field Set of the target object

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Each Quick Action has its own Action Layout that determines which fields appear on the create or update form. A controls the record detail page. C controls highlights/hover. D is a developer construct for exposing sets of fields to Visualforce and API, not action layouts.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Customize the Layouts of Object-Specific Actions

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks wants a button on the Opportunity record page that launches a screen flow to help reps qualify the deal by asking a series of questions.
questions.question: Which two options can achieve this? (Choose 2)

options.text: Create a Quick Action of type 'Flow' and add it to the Opportunity page layout / highlights panel actions
Add the Flow component to the Opportunity Lightning record page in App Builder
Create a custom URL button that redirects to /flow/QualifyOpportunity
Create a Global Action of type 'Send Email' and embed the flow

questions.explanation: The correct answers are A and B. A Flow Quick Action launches a screen flow from the record's action menu with the current recordId available. Alternatively, embedding the Flow component in App Builder embeds the flow directly on the record page. C is not the recommended path and doesn't pass the recordId contextually. D isn't a valid mechanism — Send Email doesn't launch a flow.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Add a Flow to a Lightning Page & Flow Actions

questions.scenario: AW Computing wants users to log calls quickly from any page, including the Chatter publisher, without navigating to a specific record first.
questions.question: What should the admin configure?

options.text: An object-specific Log a Call action on the Task object
A Global Log a Call action added to the Global Publisher Layout
A Custom Button on Task
A Lightning Component action

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. A Global Log a Call action, added to the Global Publisher Layout, makes call logging available from anywhere in the app, including the Chatter publisher and navigation bar. A only makes it available on Task record pages. C creates a navigation-only button, not an action to log. D would need a developer.

questions.scenario: Universal Containers wants to show or hide specific actions on the Case highlights panel based on the Case Status. For example, 'Close Case' should only appear when Status is 'Working'.
questions.question: Which feature enables this in Lightning Experience?

options.text: Page Layout with different action lists per record type
Dynamic Actions in Lightning App Builder with visibility rules
Global Action visibility settings
Apex trigger to conditionally add actions

questions.explanation: The correct answer is B. Dynamic Actions let admins add actions directly to the highlights panel in Lightning App Builder and apply visibility rules (field values, permissions, device) to control when each action appears. A allows different actions by record type but not by field value. C doesn't offer field-value-based visibility. D is programmatic and unsupported for this purpose.

questions.question: Which custom button/link type opens a Visualforce page or an external URL in the current window in Lightning Experience?

options.text: Custom URL button with the 'Display in existing window without sidebar' behavior
Global Quick Action
Publisher Action
Object-Specific Quick Action

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Custom URL buttons/links let admins launch a Visualforce page or external URL, with behavior options like current window, new window, or existing window. B, C, and D are actions used to perform in-context tasks (create/update records, log calls, launch flows) — not to navigate to a URL/VF page directly.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Define Custom Buttons and Links

questions.scenario: DreamHouse Realty's admin created an object-specific action on the Property object, but it does not appear on the Property record page for users.
questions.question: What is the most likely cause?

options.text: The action must be added to the Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions section of the Property page layout (or the highlights panel via Dynamic Actions)
The action must be created as a Global Action instead
The action must be assigned to a permission set
The action must be marked as Active in Object Manager

questions.explanation: The correct answer is A. Creating an action alone isn't enough — it must be added to the 'Salesforce Mobile and Lightning Experience Actions' section of the relevant page layout, or configured via Dynamic Actions in Lightning App Builder, before users can see it. B changes scope but doesn't solve the visibility issue. C isn't required to display an action. D isn't a valid concept for quick actions.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Add Actions to Page Layouts

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are valid Quick Action types available in Lightning Experience? (Choose 3)

options.text: Create a Record
Update a Record
Send Outbound Message
Log a Call
Execute Apex Batch

questions.explanation: The correct answers are A, B, and D. C (Send Outbound Message) is a Workflow/Flow action for integrations, not a Quick Action. E (Execute Apex Batch) is not a Quick Action type — Apex is invoked via Invocable Actions through Flow, not directly as a quick action.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Types of Quick Actions

questions.scenario: Cloud Kicks wants to add a component to the Account record page that shows the fields of the primary Contact for that Account inline.
questions.question: Which standard component should the admin use?

options.text: Related Record
Related List — Single
Record Detail
Rich Text

questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Standard Lightning Page Components — Related Record

questions.scenario: Ursa Major Solar wants a custom Lightning Web Component that its developer built to be available for admins to drag onto the Opportunity record page in Lightning App Builder.

options.text: Add lightning__RecordPage to the targets in the component's .js-meta.xml file
Deploy the component with a permission set granting App Builder access
Register the component in the App Manager
Set the component to Public in the .css file

questions.reference: Salesforce Developer Docs: Configure Components for Lightning App Builder

questions.scenario: AW Computing wants to show different Lightning components on the Opportunity record page depending on whether the user is on a phone or on a desktop.
questions.question: How should this be achieved without cloning the page?

options.text: Create two separate Lightning pages and assign one to Desktop and one to Phone
Use Component Visibility filters with Form Factor set to Phone or Desktop
Use device-specific record types
Modify the compact layout

C isn't a real feature. D governs highlights and hover, not the page body.
questions.reference: Salesforce Help: Component Visibility with Form Factor
